purpose: Colestipol is used to lower high LDL cholesterol, often called 'bad' cholesterol, in your blood. It is usually used along with a healthy diet and exercise. Keeping your cholesterol in check helps reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke.
how_it_works: Colestipol works inside your intestines by binding to bile acids, which are made from cholesterol in your liver. When it grabs onto those bile acids, your body can't reabsorb them, so they get flushed out in your stool. Your liver then has to use more cholesterol to make new bile acids, which lowers the cholesterol level in your blood.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are related to your stomach and bowels, including constipation, bloating, gas, nausea, and stomach upset. Constipation is the most frequently reported issue, especially when you first start taking it. Drinking plenty of water and eating fiber can help.
warnings: Colestipol can interfere with how your body absorbs other medications, vitamins, and nutrients, so it's important to take other drugs at least 1 hour before or 4 hours after taking colestipol. Tell your doctor if you have a history of bowel blockages, constipation problems, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It may also reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E, and K over time.
typical_dosing: Colestipol comes as tablets or granules (powder). The usual starting dose for tablets is 2 grams once or twice daily, which can be gradually increased up to 16 grams per day. The granules are typically mixed into a full glass of water or juice and taken 1 to 6 times daily. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your cholesterol levels and how well you tolerate it.
